caption: A Seneca youth, the march of the Toñwiʹsas, the women’s society of the three sisters, pen drawing printed as figure 2 in Arthur C. Parker, Iroquois Uses of Maize and Other Food Plants (1910), p. 28 (printed sideways on the page)
alt: A pen drawing of a line of Seneca women in long dresses and shawls standing in a hall lit by a hanging candle-holder; the woman in front holds an armful of corn and a round cake of bread beside a woven basket on the floor, and a group of men in feathered caps watches from the right.
bibliography: A Seneca youth. Figure 2, the march of the Toñwiʹsas. In Arthur C. Parker, Iroquois Uses of Maize and Other Food Plants, New York State Museum Bulletin 144, 1910, p. 28.
title: The march of the Toñwiʹsas
